chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever hits a bird inside the Sanctuary while he is free (not in Ihram), upon him is the price, and the price is one Dirham, which he uses to buy feed for the doves of the Sanctuary.

key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: Free from Ihram (not in the state of pilgrimage consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for hitting a bird in the Haram if not in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) specifies a fixed monetary penalty (qimah) of one Dirham for hunting birds within the Haram while in the state of Ihram, linking the compensation directly to the maintenance of the Sanctuary's doves. This ruling highlights the unique sanctity of the Haram's ecosystem and the specific legal mechanisms for preserving its religious atmosphere, as recorded in al-Kafi. The designation of funds for 'feed for the doves' underscores the practical application of these penalties in sustaining the spiritual environment of the holy site.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Safwan Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who hits a bird inside the Al-Harram and he is free (not in Ihram), so upon him is the price, and the price is one Dirham. He buys feed with it for the doves of the Al-Harram’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Safwan ibn Yahya who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If one hurts a bird in al-Haram (the sacred area) when one is not in the state of ’Ihram, he owes its price. This price is one dirham with which he buys feed for the pigeons of al-Haram (the sacred area).”’
